Person-Item Targeting Plot for the Hurdle Partial Credit Model

Source: R/brms_hpcm.R
plot_targeting_hpcm.Rd

Builds two person-item targeting plots, one for each part of a hurdle partial credit model fitted with the hurdle_acat custom family, with the same design as plot_targeting: a person histogram, an inverted histogram of the item locations, and a bottom panel with response-category bands or a dot-and-whisker plot of the thresholds. The presence part \((\theta_{hurdle}, \delta_{hurdle})\) and the severity part \((\theta_{pcm}, \tau_{ik})\) are different latent variables, so each gets its own plot and axis.

Usage

plot_targeting_hpcm(
  model,
  item_var = item,
  person_var = id,
  robust = FALSE,
  center = TRUE,
  sort_items = c("data", "location"),
  bins,
  prob = 0.95,
  palette = NULL,
  person_fill = "#0072B2",
  threshold_fill = "#D55E00",
  height_ratios = c(3, 2, 5),
  panel = c("categories", "thresholds"),
  xlim = c(-4, 4),
  category_labels = NULL,
  viridis_option = "G",
  viridis_begin = 0.9,
  viridis_end = 0.2,
  row_gap = NULL,
  output = c("patchwork", "list")
)

Arguments

model

A fitted brmsfit object using the hurdle_acat custom family.

item_var

An unquoted variable name identifying the item grouping variable in the model data. Default is item.

person_var

An unquoted variable name identifying the person grouping variable in the model data. Default is id.

robust

Logical. If TRUE, the histogram panels mark the median and MAD instead of the mean and SD. Default is FALSE.

center

Logical. If TRUE (the default), each part is shifted so that its mean item location is zero, with the person locations shifted by the same constant, as in item_parameters_hpcm and person_parameters_hpcm.

sort_items

Character. "data" (the default) keeps the data order, first item at the top. "location" sorts by mean item location, easiest item at the top.

bins

Integer. Number of histogram bins. Default as in plot_targeting.

prob

Numeric in \((0, 1)\). Width of the credible intervals of the item locations and of the intervals in the returned tables. Default is 0.95. NULL hides the intervals in the plots.

palette

An optional character vector of colours, one per response category. Overrides the viridis colours.

person_fill, threshold_fill

Fill colours for the person and item location histograms.

height_ratios

Numeric vector of length 3 giving the relative heights of the three panels. Default is c(3, 2, 5).

panel

Character. "categories" (the default) draws each item as a bar partitioned into response-category bands. "thresholds" draws a dot-and-whisker plot.

xlim

Numeric vector of length 2. Initial limits of the x-axis, widened to whole numbers if needed. Default is c(-4, 4).

category_labels

Optional list with elements hurdle (two labels) and/or pcm (one label per severity category, starting at category 1). Defaults are c("0", "1+") for the hurdle part and the category scores for the severity part.

viridis_option, viridis_begin, viridis_end

Viridis palette for the category colours, as in plot_targeting.

row_gap

Numeric. Vertical spacing between item rows in the "categories" panel. Default NULL chooses it from the number of collapsed categories and disordered thresholds.

output

Character. "patchwork" (the default) returns the two combined plots. "list" returns, for each part, the three panels and the posterior summaries of the category structure.

Value

With output = "patchwork", a list with elements hurdle and pcm, each a patchwork object. With output = "list", the same two elements, each a list with p1, p2, p3, categories and disordered as described in plot_targeting. In the severity part, categories are numbered from 1.

Details

Hurdle part. The person location is the posterior mean of the brms random effect on hu with its sign flipped, so that higher values mean a symptom is more likely to be present. The item location is the hurdle item effect, where higher values mean more zeros. Then \(P(Y_{vi} > 0) = \mathrm{plogis}(\theta_{hurdle, v} - \delta_{hurdle, i})\), a dichotomous Rasch model, and each item has two bands: 0 and any response above 0.

Severity part. The person location is the posterior mean of the random intercept, and the thresholds are those of the partial credit model for the responses above 0. The bands show the severity categories 1 and up. Persons who answered 0 on every item gave no severity responses, so their severity location comes from the prior and the correlation with the hurdle location only. They are left out of the severity person histogram, and the caption gives their number.

Category bands, red marks for categories that are never the most likely response and for disordered thresholds, and their posterior probabilities are computed as in plot_targeting.

Combining the two plots. Each element is a patchwork object:


plots <- plot_targeting_hpcm(fit)
patchwork::wrap_plots(plots$hurdle, plots$pcm, ncol = 2)

References

Wright, B. D. & Stone, M. H. (1979). Best Test Design. MESA Press.

Magnus, B. E. & Garnier-Villarreal, M. (2022). A multidimensional zero-inflated graded response model for ordinal symptom data. Psychological Methods, 27(2), 261-279. doi:10.1037/met0000395

See also

plot_targeting for the standard Rasch models, item_parameters_hpcm, person_parameters_hpcm.
